# Swing Desk status: what is confident, what is not, what is left (17 Oct 2026)

Kept current with every change. Confident means built, checked, and I would stand behind it. Not confident means it needs evidence or work before it can be trusted.

## Confident
- Dashboard and nightly India and US data jobs; the regime light (fixed, tested rules).
- Portfolio page accounting (tax, dividends, XIRR, missing-lot detection), checked on real tradebooks.
- Keep/Exit test for held stocks: replayed with split and bonus adjustment; it sorts in the right direction. It is not claimed to beat holding.
- Data plumbing: India prices 2020 to 2025 (1,439 sessions) and index history (1,436 of 1,439) loaded; as-of view passes its leak check; the US replay uses only splits known each night.
- Paper-book mechanics: tested; the official stream reproduces the C-52 replay's trades with identical returns, and adds three the replay's overlap rule or candidate filter left out.
- Process: criteria written before each run, owner marks Adopted, Rejected or Parked.

## Not confident, and how each gets there
1. **Does the US scan have an edge?** One year of data; the result was about zero once one metals rally was removed. Path: the paper book (C-53, logging from 16 Oct) read at 300 picks or 12 months, whichever is later (about Oct 2027); the India baseline (C-54) for the same signal family in days. Confident when the pre-registered pass rule holds on forward data.
2. **Does the pattern layer (pivots, setups, stop widths, room test) earn its place?** No formal evidence; it chokes on volatile stocks (extension, setup geometry, stop width; room binds once stops widen). Path: the three paper-book streams isolate stop width and entry; later the funnel is tested against the plain baseline on six India years. If it cannot beat the baseline, simplify.
3. **Is "swing" the right holding period?** Path: the 20, 60 and 120-session curve in C-54. Days after confirmation.
4. **Does the funnel beat plain momentum?** The India scan is now built and frozen (IND-SCAN-1, 17 Oct, forward log only; pre-registration docs/replay/IND-SCAN-1-PREREG.md). Next: a registered test (C-57) against the C-54 baseline, and a replay once the longer history is in.
5. **India corporate-action list.** Cleared by written rules 17 Oct: 72 of the 76 liquid unexplained breaks (splits, demergers, genuine falls); the 4 left were settled the same day from public sources and are typed in corp-action-overrides-hist.json (one special dividend, two bonuses, one demerger). Factors are rule-derived approximations, not checked against announcements; see docs/replay/INDIA-BREAKS-CLEARED-2026-10-17.md. Path to confidence: check the demerger factors that matter (Siemens, Raymond, ABFRL) against company notices.
6. **Cost assumptions** (India 0.35 / 0.50 / 0.80% round trip). Checked 17 Oct against data/rules/charges.json: statutory plus brokerage is 0.23 to 0.29% round trip for positions of Rs 1 to 5 lakh (0.23 to 0.24% on the cheaper of the two broker schedules in the file, 0.24 to 0.29% on the other), of which 0.20% is STT; small orders on the second schedule cost more (0.36% at Rs 50,000, 0.49% at Rs 25,000) because of the Rs 20 brokerage and DP fee. So the 0.25% statutory part holds for normal sizes. The slippage part (0.10 / 0.25 / 0.55%) is still a guess, not measured; C-54's fit result already holds at double cost. Path: compare fill prices in your tradebooks with the day's VWAP once the files are loaded.
7. **Scan weights 60/25/15.** Signed off, untested. Path: leave frozen; read the paper book's top-10 log; a report-only equal-weight check once the India scan exists. No tuning.
8. **C-54 result: inconclusive (run 17 Oct).** Strong in the fit window (2021 to 2023: +151% against +66% Nifty 500), gave it all back in the holdout (2024 to Sep 2025: +10% against +19%; 2025 alone -20% against a flat index). Momentum is real in some regimes and cyclical with the small-cap cycle, not a free lunch. Path: extend the history back to about 2010 (older NSE file format and a corporate-action source before 2019) so the test sees more cycles.

## Known defects in the existing build
- **US scan was two sessions late (closed).** The free Massive plan posts a day's whole-market file the next evening. FIXED 17 Oct (C-55): the official scan runs the same evening (about 22:45 ET) from the Nasdaq-sourced store; the Massive scan stays as a cross-check. Checked 20 Oct: latest scan is dated 19 Oct, source nasdaq. Listed names only, so every US test states the survivorship bias.
- **Actions minutes (open, watching; one reading a day).** Re-read 19 Oct from billed job time: 1,681 of 2,000 used (the earlier 1,787 counted queue wait). About 12 days to go with roughly 320 left, and the steady weekday cost is about 55 (ticks 26, nightlies 8, ci 15 to 25). Done 19 Oct: ci cancels superseded runs and skips replay notes and STATUS; fund-scores moved from weekly to monthly; the tick's commit step was failing because the dashboard rebuild left unstaged files (fixed); the usage total now comes from a per-run file (data/ops/usage-jobs.json) because the runs list only reaches back 1,000 runs. Done by the owner 19 Oct (cron-job.org): A India `7 14-15,17 * * 1-5` (19:37 IST start, one retry, 22:37 IST alert check); B US evening disabled; C US late and India morning kept at `7,37 0-4 * * 2-6` (it starts the US daily feed, breadth and scan; 1 Nov DST moves them an hour later in UTC and the window still covers it). 13 tick runs a weekday instead of 26, saving about 13 minutes a day. If the reading is still too high, C can start at hour 1 (2 fewer a day). 21 Oct 21:23 IST: GitHub's own billing page shows 1,971 of 2,000 used (our per-run count said about 1,870, so the estimate runs about 5% low); ci is now manual-only (workflow_dispatch). LIFTED 21 Oct 22:53 IST: the owner made the code repo public (unlimited minutes), so ci runs on pushes again and the hold on fetches and backfills is over. 21 Oct: C-80 settled the four open rule questions from the strategy and data (see Engine Rules). ci now also skips docs/**, *.md, site/data and site/pm-data; pushes are batched to one a day until 1 Nov; budget reading 1,860 of 2,000 (140 left, steady weekday about 21 minutes); DONE by the owner 21 Oct: C now `7,37 1-3 * * 2-6` (4 fewer ticks a day, about 17 minutes a weekday). Nothing else in the repo can go below one billed minute per tick. 22 Oct: the owner restored C to `7,37 0-4 * * 2-6` (the repo is public, minutes are unlimited). 22 Oct: the cleaned history was published and the private rules moved to the private repo; Engine Rules copy re-exported at doc rev 226.

## Pending scope of work, in order
**Owner decisions:** whether the Portfolio Manager design doc may appear on the desk (and SCOPE). Decided 17 Oct: US long history from Nasdaq's public API, listed names only (survivorship bias disclosed in every test); no purchase.

**Multiple scan strategies (owner request, 20 Oct):** not started; proposed shape and an open question in SCOPE.md. Needs the owner's choice of strategies.
**Portfolio Manager:** verdicts (200 SMA, swing low), relative strength rank, segment tag and the nightly context refresh are built and shown on the Upload and Holdings page. Built 19 Oct: next results date for each held stock (NSE announced board-meeting dates, `site/pm-data/results-next.json`) in the stock's detail row, and a "Results due within 10 sessions" line on the What to do card; information only, no rule change. Built 20 Oct: the Market tab holdings card (see below) and a second source for results dates: NSE's whole-market event calendar, saved nightly by scan-earnings (data/india/scan/results-calendar.json) and merged by build-pm-site (the fresher date wins; disagreements are listed under `differs` in results-next.json). BSE was probed and refuses the runners (Access Denied), so it is not an option. Takes effect from tonight's India scan run. Built 20 Oct (phase 5): the allocation engine (`src/pm/allocation.ts`, settings in `settings/allocation.json`, mapping in `src/pm/assetclass.ts`) and an Allocation tab on the Portfolio page: capital, risk profile (Cautious, Balanced, Aggressive, Custom), horizon in years, optional liquidity buffer and which of the ten asset classes are on give a target per class, set against what is held, with the drift band, the rule behind each number and the single-stock and single-fund limits. Equity share glides continuously with the horizon. Two tests run on every input combination (`test/pm-allocation.test.ts`): targets add to 100% within every cap or a plain message names the clash; a one-notch input change moves targets by a bounded amount. After an external review (20 Oct) three values changed: gold share of non-equity 25% to 20% (the default no longer hits the gold maximum), the drawdown limit is now equity share x 40% assumed bear-market fall instead of a flat figure, and the hybrid fold for balanced advantage, dynamic asset allocation and equity savings counts unhedged equity (40% and 25%). A randomised 20,000-input test was added. Phase 7 part 1 built 20 Oct (`src/pm/swingpools.ts`, `test/pm-swingpools.test.ts`, a Swing pools card on the Allocation tab for a household with two or more accounts): swing capital per account is derived (the household swing target x the account's share of what the household holds), the position cap and the one-stock-one-account rule are checked across accounts, and the card names the account where the next new swing trade would go (already held, then cash, then tax, then fewer positions). (household-specific detail kept in the private repository) Tax routing needs owners assigned to the accounts. Not built: the nightly Swing shortlist does not yet use the account split, open-risk limits are not shown, and the source of capital is one setting, not a per-account record. Per-account allocation built 20 Oct (owner request): every account has its own capital to allocate, risk profile, horizon, buffer, new money, scope and custom weights (saved with the account, see the next entry); the household view is the sum of the accounts' own targets and holdings (`rollUp` in `src/pm/allocation.ts`), and swing capital per account is now the account's own swing target x its own capital, not a share of a household figure. Old single-set inputs are ignored. Phase 7 finished and phase 6 gaps closed 20 Oct. Tonight's swing orders by account (`src/pm/swingorders.ts`, `test/pm-swingorders.test.ts`, card on the Allocation tab for a household): the public nightly plan (trigger, stop, setup from the India scan and paper book) is sized in the browser for each account on that account's own swing capital using the Swing Desk's own sizing (`ntCalc`) and the rules table for today's market light (India VIX above 20 halves risk), with the binding constraint shown per account (one R of risk, 20% position cap, the account's open-risk limit, the household open-risk limit, household position count, a short-term Legacy lot blocking the stock, a setup not allowed on the light) and routed by the existing order (already held, tax, fewer positions, more room). Holdings never leave the browser, so nothing private reaches data/. Open risk needs a stop for each open Swing position: typed once under the card (stored in the browser); until then open risk is understated and the card says so. Not applied there (they need the trade journal): sector pilot sizing, proven-Green 1%, risk halving. Phase 6 gaps: exit loads (`data/rules/exit-loads.json`, typed with evidence; empty because the sandbox cannot reach AMC sites; a fund with no record bought in the last year is flagged to check; known loads count toward cost and those lots sell last); quarterly cap (press 'I acted on' for a class; no new sale suggestion for it that quarter unless drift passes twice the band); slab-rate tax (rate typed per account, kept in the browser; priced into slab-rate lines); fund Replace/Exit sales are wired but switched OFF (`rebalance.fundVerdictSales` false) because the fund-score back-test required by design 9.1 has not run and Exit needs structural data that does not exist yet. New settings values are PROPOSED, for the owner to confirm. [private note kept out of the public repo]  Swing recognition built 20 Oct (owner: a trade can be near a setup without matching it exactly): the nightly India shortlist is now saved (`data/india/shortlist/<date>.json`, from `scripts/save-shortlist.mjs`; line = symbol, setup, stream, trigger, limit, stop, ATR %, desk tags; two nights back-filled from the paper book). A real buy is EXACT (entry session, inside trigger and limit, a calm stock, a line the desk did not tag over cap or room fail): Swing automatically with that line's stop and setup. It is NEAR (up to 3 weekdays later, or up to 2% outside the range; a stock with ATR above 3% may fill up to 5% above the limit, because its entry waits for a confirming close; a line tagged over cap or room fail is always near): proposed on the Data tab, Swing only on the owner's yes, answer saved with the account. Otherwise Legacy. Numbers are approved working values (settings/allocation.json swingMatch; Engine Rules C-76), untested until 40 shortlist nights exist. Two independent reviewers (logic; security and persistence) found 20-odd issues the same day; fixed: volatile entries, rejected paper lines, settings failing open, per-account running open risk and position cap within a night, account rename and delete losing inputs, parallel and stale saves (settings now saved as a per-key patch, one save at a time per account, retry on a lost race), ghost accounts, null body, CI no longer runs for portfolio/ saves. The six gaps the reviewers left were closed the same day (owner: build all and close it): (1) a sale of a stock after a Swing buy is put to the owner ("was this your Swing exit?"); yes moves those units out of the Swing book, the tax view stays oldest-first; (2) a second order of the same stock the same day, or a later add within 12 sessions of a matched buy (the rules add only at the first +1R close, and the 10-session time stop sells a trade with none), is proposed as part of that trade; (3) an exact match above 6% of the account's value is only a near match; (4) sessions skip exchange holidays and count extra sessions (data/calendar); (5) the job now writes data/india/shortlist/index.json (nights it ran, go-live date) and the desk names nights the job missed; (6) passages wrapped in private markers are removed from the published copy of this page (scripts/strip-private.mjs). The owner approved 6% and 12 sessions on 20 Oct; the near-match numbers (3 sessions, 2%, 5%) stay PROVISIONAL, Engine Rules C-76. Swing journal from real trades built 20 Oct (owner request; Engine Rules C-77, Proposed): every buy recognised as Swing (exact, or near and confirmed) becomes a trade, open or closed, grouped by stock and buy date, with its sells from the broker data (plus sales you confirm as your Swing exit). It is scored with the Swing Desk's own maths (`src/engine/journal.ts`): R on the units bought gross of charges, equity on Swing trades only starting from the household's swing capital, risk halving (three losses in a row, or equity 5% below peak), and the Journal Test (20 closed trades over 90 days; expectancy +0.3R, average loss 1.2R, rule breaks 2 or fewer in the last 20, drawdown under 8%). A card on the Allocation tab shows it; halving and the proven-Green 1% feed tonight's order sizes for a household of two or more accounts. You answer Yes or No per closed trade for 'rules followed' (broker data cannot show it); an unanswered trade blocks the Rule breaks test, and proven Green is also blocked while sale or near-match questions are open, sells cannot be explained, or a trade is left out after a split or demerger. Not measured: MAE, MFE, charges, slippage against a planned fill. A trade whose stock had a split, demerger or rename after the buy is left out and named. An independent review the same day found 10 issues; fixed: a stopped-out trade dropping out when the account shrinks, a closed trade offered as the base of an add, mixed units after corporate events, same-day fill order, the answer cap (now 2,000) and wording. Not fixed: the single-account household gets the journal card but no order sizing card. Trades tab built 20 Oct (owner request: all trade history, not only Swing): every buy and sell in the statements for stocks, ETFs and funds (`src/pm/tradehistory.ts`, `test/pm-tradehistory.test.ts`), shown four ways with one set of filters (account, type, book, open or closed, year, search by name): a table with one row per holding that opens to its buys and sells, a monthly timeline, a card per stock, and a chart of realised profit by month with best and worst holdings. Realised gain on each sale is the Tax tab's oldest-first figure, so the two agree. Display only: no rule uses it and nothing new is stored. Units held and the status (Open, Partly sold, Closed) come from the tax replay, so bonuses, splits and demergers do not make a stock look closed; a stock with no buy in the statements (units that arrived by demerger, bonus or grant) is flagged and its cost and first date are unknown; funds the AMFI list cannot match are listed too, from their trades. Each sale's gain follows its own price within a same-day group. An independent review found 8 points the same day; fixed all but: a phone shows the holding table scrolled sideways, and the Account, Book and Last sold columns are not hidden on small screens. Limits: a stock renamed or demerged is shown under the key the statements use, so its history can split across two names; the book shown is where the holding sits now (a stock that is both Swing and Legacy shows both). Trade review built 20 Oct (owner request: learn what went well and what did not): a Review view on the Trades tab (`src/pm/tradereview.ts`, `test/pm-tradereview.test.ts`). For every holding that has been sold it states the result on the units sold against the Nifty 50 index fund over the same days, the 20-session run-up before the buy, the buy against the year's high, the worst dip and best run while held, how much of the best gain was given back, and what the stock did in the 20 sessions after the sale, from the stored split-adjusted daily closes (since April 2021), then lists what went well and what did not and gives a one-word grade (Went well = a profit that kept up with the index; Mixed = a profit behind the index; Did not go well = a loss). Swing trades are also checked against the planned stop (a loss near 1R is as planned; past 1.25R is not) and your rules-followed answer. The Review card follows the account chosen in the side list (one account, one person's accounts, or the household): with more than one account it shows a table with each account and a total row (sold holdings, how many went well, mixed or not, share at a profit, how many beat the Nifty 50, average days held, realised), and the patterns below are for the selection. A card on top states patterns across trades (winners against losers holding days, late entries, giving back gains, selling early, beating the index) only when each group has at least 5 trades. Funds are reviewed only when fund NAVs are switched on. A stock whose history has a split or demerger the stored prices cannot adjust, one with no buy in the statements, or one with no symbol is left out of the entry and exit checks and counted. The wording thresholds (20% run-up, 15% dip, half the gain given back, 15% rise after the sale) are display choices, not trading rules. Commentary only: nothing here changes any rule or any order size. Trade review extended 20 Oct (owner: what went wrong, what a stop would have saved, why I bought): each sold holding now also shows a main issue for a loss (held while falling, chased an entry, the market fell, sold near the low, or unclear; picked from the numbers in that order), a stop-loss what-if (a fixed stop 8%, 10% or 15% under the buy-day close, sold at the first close past it, in rupees on the units sold: money saved on trades that kept falling, and money it would have cost on trades that dipped through the stop and then recovered), and what the market was doing when you bought (change in the 5 and 20 sessions before, distance from the year's high, buy-day volume against the 50-day average, delivery %) with a plain read (chasing a move, breakout, volume-driven, dip buy, or no sign of chasing). The reason in your head is not in the data, so the read is a hint and says so. Stocks bought or sold the same day as others in the account are flagged as one decision. The top card adds the stop what-if totals across all reviewed trades (saved, cost, net) and patterns for volume spikes and main issues. Volume and delivery come from new monthly files (`site/pm-data/volume/`, built from the daily bhavcopy store from January 2021; closed months are not rebuilt) loaded only for the months a review needs. Stop levels and read thresholds are display choices, not rules. Tactical tilt tested 20 Oct (C-74): letting the allocation move with market performance (a monthly trend tilt on equity, international, gold and silver, bounded per profile) did NOT beat static weights in the fit period (Balanced -0.8pp a year, Aggressive -2.0pp after costs); holdout not revealed; no tilt built; re-run on the longer India history after 1 Nov (docs/replay/TACTICAL-TILT-2026-10-20.md). Sector rotation tested 20 Oct (C-75): holding the top two sectors that pass the Swing Desk sector gate, monthly, did NOT beat the Nifty 500 in the fit period (-1.0pp a year after costs, drawdown 36.7% against 18.5%); holdout not revealed; sector and thematic funds stay at 0% in the presets, available only through the Custom profile (docs/replay/SECTOR-ROTATION-2026-10-20.md). Phase 6 built 20 Oct (rebalancing and new-money sizing, `src/pm/rebalance.ts`, `test/pm-rebalance.test.ts`, a Suggested actions card on the Allocation tab): new money is routed first to the classes furthest below target; only a class still above target plus band is sold down, from lots in this order: Exit-verdict names, loss lots, long-term equity (exemption), other long-term, short-term; never the Swing book, locked ELSS or unclassified holdings; each line shows account, units, gain, estimated tax and charges; sales below the minimum trade (Rs 10,000) or costing more than 3% of the sale are skipped (settings/allocation.json, `rebalance`; owner to confirm these two). Not built: exit loads (no data), the one-suggestion-per-class-per-quarter cap (needs a stored decision log), slab-rate tax figures (slab rate not set), hybrid-fund sales, funds' Exit or Replace verdicts as sale triggers. The owner approved the allocation values on 20 Oct. ELSS units bought in the last 3 years are shown as locked (counted, not sellable). The lock figure is computed from purchase dates and is not yet checked against real holdings.  Targets only: no orders (rebalancing and new-money sizing are phase 6). Deviation from the design text: the asset-class mapping lives in code (category and name rules), not in `settings/instruments.json`; unmatched holdings show as not classified and are left out of totals.
**Pending scope of work (recorded 21 Oct 2026 after the four-way audit):** the full list of what the design promises and is not built (Trim, Promote and Harvest verdicts, fund verdicts and shortlist, Schedule CG export, holdings-snapshot gate, INDmoney and US adapters, Liquidity book, sector and country caps, tax gaps, reader learning, Corrections screen, phase 9) is in docs/SCOPE.md section J. Accepted by the owner: the saved accounts live under `portfolio/` in the private repo and the privacy check does not scan that folder.
**Fund overlap and look-through (phase 8, Engine Rules C-78, built 21 Oct 2026):** The Allocation tab has a card, "What you really own · funds opened up": for each company, what is held directly plus each equity fund's value times that company's weight in its latest monthly portfolio, as a percent of capital; pairs of funds that repeat each other (overlap = smaller weights added up, flagged at 40%); a flag when a company goes above the single-stock limit. Portfolios come from a monthly workflow (`fund-holdings`, 12th of the month, also manual) that reads the equity lines from each Direct mutual and index fund's public page and writes `data/funds/holdings.json` (about 1.8 MB, keyed by scheme name without plan words, so a Regular plan uses its Direct plan's portfolio). A page is stored only if its scheme code equals the fund's AMFI code; a failed fetch keeps last month's portfolio. Funds with no portfolio, weights over 105% (arbitrage and similar), hybrid, debt, gold and international are left out and named, never estimated; coverage is shown. Companies are matched by normalised name, so a fund line for a company not held directly keeps its own name. Nothing personal is stored in the repo: the maths runs in the browser. Files: `src/pm/lookthrough.ts`, `src/pm/holdingsparse.ts`, `scripts/fetch-holdings.mjs`, `scripts/probe-holdings.mjs` (one-off probe that picked the source), tests `test/pm-lookthrough.test.ts`, `test/pm-holdingsparse.test.ts`. ETFs are opened too (21 Oct): their pages list companies by ISIN only, so names and symbols come from the NSE listed-companies file, and the page carries no portfolio date, so the fetch date stands in. **Held funds are opened on demand too (21 Oct):** a held equity fund or ETF that is not in the monthly file is looked up when the card is shown, by its own ISIN and AMFI code, through `/api/fundport` (behind the same login; one cached answer per fund per day); a wrong-scheme page is refused, and a fund that cannot be found is named with the reason. This route runs from the Cloudflare worker and has NOT been tried from there (the sandbox cannot reach the source); if the source blocks the worker, the card says so per fund and the monthly file still applies. Not built: hybrid funds' real equity/debt mix, debt and international look-through, a full (not top 12) list with search. The source is a third-party site's page data, not an official feed; if its layout changes the log (`data/funds/holdings-log.json`) shows the drop and the card falls back to "not covered".

# Swing Desk – Engine Rules (Source of Truth)

Oct 3, 2026 · @Owner

## How to use this document

This is the single source of truth for what the Swing Desk decides and why. If the code and this document disagree, this document is right and the code has a bug.

**Rules version:** R-2026.10.9 (R-2026.10.8 plus the removal of the India skipped-days wording, adopted 20 Oct 2026, C-73; R-2026.10.8 was R-2026.10.7 plus the sector zero-return test adopted 17 Oct 2026, C-58; R-2026.10.7 was R-2026.10.6 plus the automatic handling of untyped demergers adopted 15 Oct 2026, C-50; R-2026.10.6 was R-2026.10.5 plus the Legacy exit-test definition adopted 15 Oct 2026, C-41; R-2026.10.5 was the Swing Desk app v9 as of 3 Oct 2026, after two reviews, plus three corrections found in the third review, C-35 to C-37, and the Red setup list, OQ-8. The live Claude desk was patched to v9.1 on 3 Oct 2026 and now follows these rules, except that it counts weekdays and not exchange holidays until the GitHub build adds the calendar, C-39). Every rule change bumps this number and adds a row to the Change log.

**The change rule:**

1. Write the proposed change in the Change log first, with status Proposed, the reason and the evidence that motivates it.
2. Test it (backtest, replay or paper trade) and record the result in the same row.
3. Mark it Adopted, Rejected or Parked. Only Adopted changes edit the rule text above.
4. Change the code, then record the code version in the row, and re-export this document to docs/ENGINE\_RULES.md in the repo in the same commit. The Code and Architecture document is updated in the same step if data, settings or structure changed.

Rejected ideas stay in the log permanently so nobody re-tests them without new evidence.

**Scope:** the rules apply to both markets. Where India and the US differ, the difference is shown in a per-market table and the reason is given. Parameters live in settings files, never inside the code (see the Code and Architecture document). 

**Precedence between documents:** this document wins over every other. The app's Rules tab (the playbook) is the trader-facing manual derived from the current rules version, and the Master Rules document and the scope of work are inputs and plans. If any of them disagree with this document, this document is right and the other one is updated, never the reverse.

## Principles

The desk is built on risk first, momentum second, and as little discretion as possible.

- **Market first.** The regime traffic light decides how much risk is allowed at all. A strong stock in a Red market is still a small position or no position.
- **Leaders in leading sectors.** Money is made in the strongest sectors and the strongest stocks inside them. Weak sectors are not traded.
- **Fixed risk per trade.** Every position is sized from the stop distance so a stop-out costs a fixed fraction of capital.
- **Rules decide, the trader executes.** The tool tells the trader what is allowed. It does not place orders.
- **Data accuracy beats rule cleverness.** A rule fed wrong numbers is worse than a simple rule fed right ones. Every number carries its source and date, and stale data blocks a decision rather than being silently used.
- **Same logic for both markets.** India and the US share one rule set. Differences are parameters, each with a stated reason.
- **Nothing is changed without a log entry.** See the change rule above.

## Regime traffic light

The regime is Green, Yellow or Red, computed on the market benchmark (India: Nifty; US: SPY) and taking the worst of the tests below.

| Test | Rule | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trend | Benchmark above both 50 and 200 SMA and the 50 SMA rising | Green. Above one average and below the other, or 50 SMA not rising: Yellow. Below both: Red |
| Distribution days | 5 or more in the last 25 sessions | Caps the regime at Yellow |
| Breadth | Share of stocks above their 50 SMA below 40% | Caps the regime at Yellow |
| Follow-through day | A confirmed follow-through day after a correction | Lifts Red to Yellow |
| Volatility (India) | India VIX above 20 | Halves the risk per trade |

**Exact definitions (from app v9):**

- **Benchmarks:** India uses Nifty 50 and Nifty 500; US uses SPY and QQQ. Each is read as Green (above 50 and 200 SMA, 50 rising), Mixed (above one average and below the other, or 50 SMA not rising) or Red (below both). The trend level is the lower of the two.
- **Distribution day:** the index closes down 0.2% or more on higher volume than the previous non-skipped session (a skipped day's volume is never the baseline, C-36). A day drops out after 25 sessions, or earlier if the index closes 5% above that day's close. Five or more active days cap the regime at Yellow. The US uses SPY volume with no expiry adjustment.
- **Skipped days:** none, in either market. The engine can skip a flagged day (the skip field on a tracker row), but no day is flagged: every session counts for distribution and follow-through, as in the US. C-72 (20 Oct 2026) tested excluding India's monthly expiry, Muhurat and after-holiday sessions and found no improvement, so the earlier India skip list was dropped (C-73).
- **Follow-through day:** after the index makes a new low, day 1 is the first close above the previous day's high. On day 4 or later, a close up 1.25% or more on higher volume than the previous session is the follow-through day. A new low before that restarts the count. Follow-through is only looked for inside a correction. The correction tracker arms when the benchmark closes 8% or more below its highest close of the last 60 sessions, or when the trend test reads Red (below both its 50 and 200 SMA), whichever comes first; it disarms when the benchmark closes above that 60-session high again. At arming, the low is the lowest low since the 60-session closing high, and day 1 and the day count are worked out from that low over the stored rows, not from the arming day; so a follow-through on the arming day itself is valid, and the rally-low failure test uses that seeded low and is never set above the true low. If a new low forms after arming, it replaces the seeded one and restarts the count. All follow-through state is cleared when the tracker disarms. A follow-through lifts Red to Yellow and nothing else: if the tracker is armed but the trend is Yellow, it is recorded and changes nothing. The 8% and 60 sessions are untested starting values (C-35).
- **Follow-through status:** Active when it happens, Confirmed when breadth goes above 50%, Failed if the index closes below the rally low or breadth has not passed 50% within 10 sessions. Sessions, here and everywhere in these rules, are counted on the market calendar: weekends and exchange holidays are not sessions (C-37). Active or Confirmed lifts Red to Yellow.
- **Breadth:** the share of a stock universe whose close is above its own 50-day average, in percent to one decimal. India: the Nifty 500 (NSE's current list) on stored NSE closes. US: the S&P 500 (the S5FI definition) on Nasdaq's public history. A stock needs 50 sessions of history and is left out (counted as skipped) when any one-day move inside its 50-day window is beyond 22%, which marks an unadjusted split or bonus. Today's list is used for past days, so past breadth carries survivorship bias. Below 40% caps the regime at Yellow.
- **India VIX:** above 20 halves risk per trade.

## Sector ranking

Only sectors that pass the gate are ranked, and only the top four are tradable that week (top two in Yellow).

1. **Gate.** The sector's 3-month return beats the benchmark's 3-month return, the sector's own 3-month return is above zero (C-58), and the sector is above its 50 SMA. In Red mode the 50 SMA test is dropped; the two 3-month tests still apply. A sector that is falling, but falling less than a falling benchmark, does not pass.
2. **Score.** 2 × 3-month return + 1-month return. Highest score ranks first.
3. **Top four** are kept each weekend.
4. **Confirmed or early.** Above the 200 SMA is confirmed (full size). Below it is early (pilot size only).
5. **Persistence.** A sector must appear in the top four on two consecutive weekends before it earns full trust. A new leader (a sector that jumps from outside the top 8 into the top 4 within three weeks) that has not yet persisted may be traded as a pilot only.
6. **Concentration.** Maximum 2 open positions per industry and 3 per sector.

**Data basis.** India sector returns and SMAs come from the official NSE index close file. US sector returns come from stored unadjusted closes. The US 200 SMA is computed from those stored closes, which can sit up to about 1.3% below published dividend-adjusted averages for dividend-paying ETFs. This is expected and is not a data error (see Change log C-14).

## Stock selection

Stocks are only considered inside sectors that rank in the current top group.

**US candidate screen (live in app v9, run weekly):**

| Test | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Pool | Top 10 holdings of each sector ETF in the top group (Yellow: 2 sectors, Green: 4) |
| Trend | Close above 50 and 200 SMA, and 50 SMA above 200 SMA |
| Leads its sector | 1-month return at least equal to its sector ETF's 1-month return |
| Liquidity | Average daily dollar volume of $50 million or more |
| Results | Next results date more than 10 trading days away. Unknown date is flagged, never passed |
| Setup and room | A permitted setup is in place, stop width is within the setup's limit, and there are 3R of room to the 50-day high |
| Freshness | Stock data dated before the screen date is excluded |

A stock is **Ready** when every test passes and **Watch** when trend, liquidity and results pass but no setup, room, stop width or relative strength is in place. The trader still checks the 3-month relative-strength line against SPY on the chart before buying. 

**India stock scan (Chartink, manual until the GitHub build):** the Minervini trend template: close above 150 and 200 SMA, 150 above 200, 200 SMA rising versus a month ago, 50 SMA above 150 and 200, close above 50, at least 30% above the 52-week low and within 25% of the 52-week high, traded value over ₹10 crore a day, price over ₹50, market cap over ₹1,000 crore.

**Known limits:** the US screen uses 50-session highs and lows, not a full year. It reads holdings of the ETFs only, so smaller stocks outside the sector indexes are not found until the whole-market scan is built (Parked item P-1).

**Target rule (not yet built, see Change log C-20):** one trend template for both markets, applied to the whole liquid universe each night, with a relative-strength percentile rank. India and US use the same tests with different liquidity floors.

## Setups and entry calculation

| Id | Setup | Trigger above basis | Limit above trigger | Max stop width | Basis price | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Base breakout | 0.5% | 1% | 8% | Pivot (top of the base) | Stop: low of the last tight area |
| 1ipo | IPO base breakout | 0.5% | 1% | 10% | Pivot (top of the IPO base) | Listed 30 or more sessions ago (no IPO in its first 30 trading days) |
| 2 | Pullback to 20 EMA | 0.2% | 1% | 7% | High of the day that closed at or above the 20 EMA | Stop: pullback low. Skip if the pullback closes below the 50 SMA |
| 3 | Earnings gap | 0.2% | 1.5% | 8% | Gap-day high | Stop: gap-day low. Exempt from the results-date test. Not used in the US |
| 4 | Pullback to 50 SMA | 0.2% | 1% | 6% | High of the holding day | Stop: lowest low of the pullback. Skip if the pullback closes below the 50 SMA |

**Entry calculation (function ntCalc in app v9):**

1. Trigger price = basis price × (1 + trigger %). The basis is the pivot for a breakout or the pullback high for a pullback.
2. Limit price = trigger × (1 + limit %). Orders above the limit are not chased.
3. Stop = the setup's structural stop (US screen: the lowest low of the last 10 sessions). If that stop is closer than 1.5 × ATR(14) below entry, it is widened to entry − 1.5 ATR so ordinary noise does not stop the trade out.
4. Stop width must not exceed the setup's maximum. If it does, the trade is skipped, not resized.
5. Room: distance from entry to the nearest overhead resistance must be at least 3R in the US and 2R in India. A breakout with no overhead resistance passes (in the manual checklist, a resistance level of 0 or at or below the entry means none above).
6. Results: the next results date must be more than 10 trading days away.
7. Size comes from the sizing section below.

Why the markets differ: the US room test is 3R against India's 2R because of the tax cost of US stocks. A trade must clear a bigger gain before the tax drag is worth it (stated by the owner, 3 Oct 2026). Setup 3 (earnings gap) is skipped in the US because US results gaps of 20% happen and a stop cannot act overnight (C-25). The 3R test also covers the extra brokerage and slab-rate tax.

## Position sizing and limits per market

Shares = (capital × risk per trade) ÷ (entry − stop), then limited to 20% of capital per position. India VIX above 20 halves the risk per trade.

**India**

| Regime | Setups allowed | Sectors traded | Risk per trade | Max positions | Max open risk (new trades) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Green | 1, 1ipo, 2, 3, 4 | top 4 | 0.5% | 10 | 5% |
| Yellow | 1, 1ipo, 3, 4 | top 2 | 0.5% | 5 | 2.5% |
| Red | 1, 4 | top 4 | 0.25% | 2 | 0.5% |

**US**

| Regime | Setups allowed | Sectors traded | Risk per trade | Max positions | Max open risk (new trades) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Green | 1, 1ipo, 2, 4 | top 4 | 0.5% | 4 | 2% |
| Yellow | 1, 1ipo, 4 | top 2 | 0.5% | 4 | 2% |
| Red | 1, 4 | top 4 | 0.25% | 2 | 0.5% |

Values are copied from LIMITS and LIMITS\_US in app v9. The last column is the maximum total open risk for new trades, because the code compares open risk against capital times this percentage. It is not a position cap; the position cap is 20% of capital (next section). In Red the playbook allows pilots only, and the checklist enforces that, so the setup list for Red is setups 1 and 4 only, in both markets (owner decision 3 Oct 2026, OQ-8 closed; app v9 let Red accept every setup) (C-24, C-38).

A stock scoring Ready on the US screen is still sized by the normal New trade checklist; the screen never sizes a trade.

## Entry mechanics and book rules

These rules were already in app v9 but missing from this document until the 3 Oct 2026 review.

- **Two-part entry:** buy 60% of full size at the trigger. Add the other 40% after a close at +1R and move the stop on all shares to entry. If the first +1R close is already at +2R or higher (a gap), skip the add and sell the third under exit rule 5. Adds do not count toward the daily entry cap.
- **Pilot size:** risk is capped at 0.25% when the sector is a new leader that has not yet persisted, when the stock is a bottom-up leader (3 or more stocks of one industry passing the scans) in a sector that has not persisted, when the sector is below its 200 SMA (early), and in every Red market. A bottom-up leader skips the sector rank, persistence and 200 SMA checks (the industry evidence stands in for them) and trades at pilot size until its sector persists.
- **Red path:** a Red-market trade needs an RS leader (India: top 20% of Nifty 500 on 3- or 6-month return; US: RS line against SPY rising or at a new high) trading above its own 50 SMA, and one of the setups.
- **Entry order type: if ATR is above 3% of price, skip the intraday standing buy order. If the stock closes above the pivot in the top half of its day's range, place a limit buy at that close + 1% the next morning (India: an after-market order, AMO; US: a limit buy) and skip the trade if it does not fill. Never use a market order for a buy. In the trade record, method is amo for this close-confirmed entry and gtt otherwise. The stop is always a standing order placed the same evening as the fill**.
- **Daily cap:** at most two new entries a day, highest RS first.
- **Position cap:** no position above 20% of capital, even if the risk formula says more.
- **Sector rank:** the stock's sector must be in the top 4 (top 2 in Yellow).
- **Legacy book (India long-term holdings):** the exit test is a close below the 200 SMA or below the last major swing low. The last major swing low is the most recent confirmed pivot low on daily closes: a close that is the lowest of the 10 sessions on each side of it, confirmed only after 10 later sessions. The 200 SMA is the mean of the last 200 closes. Closes are first adjusted for splits, bonuses, large dividends, rights and demergers (a typed record that passes the price check first; otherwise a fall of 15% or more across the ex-date is used as the factor, and a smaller one drops the closes before the ex-date, C-44, C-50). The test gives no verdict where an action in the last 300 sessions cannot be adjusted, the latest close is over 7 days old, or fewer than 200 sessions exist and the swing low is not broken; a stock with fewer than 200 sessions that closes below its swing low is still an Exit, labelled as swing-low only (C-41). A passing holding gets a stop just under the higher of the swing low and the 200 SMA, and is trimmed until the drop from price to stop is at most 1% of capital and no holding exceeds 20% of capital. The legacy book has its own 3% open-risk budget, separate from new trades, and the 10-stock maximum is the target for the whole book. Trims sell the oldest lots first (FIFO), so loss lots book a tax loss first. Legacy trailing (copied from the app Rules tab, OQ-7): kept winners follow the week-8 trail rules from day one. Every weekend, raise each legacy stop to the higher of the 10-week average and the last swing low. Exit on a weekly close below the 10-week average (rule 6) and sell a third on a climax (rule 7). Stops never move down. Tighten first, trim second: if the combined give-back is above 3% of capital, first tighten stops to the 10-week-average level; trim only if the book is still above 3% after that, starting with the largest single give-back. The give-back is the combined drop from today's prices to the stops across all kept holdings; a holding whose stop is above its cost puts no capital at risk. The legacy book does not count toward the open-risk cap for new trades, but it counts toward the 10-stock book. Concentration applies to it too: kept holdings count toward 3 per sector and 2 per industry. For a crowded group keep at most three, the strongest on the exit test, and on a tie sell first those whose tax is already covered. 

**Risk halving:** risk per trade halves automatically after three closed new trades in a row below 0R, or while new-trade equity is 5% or more below its peak (that case ends when equity recovers); the three-losses case ends after two winners close. India VIX above 20 halves it again.

**Checklist rules not stated elsewhere:** every trade needs an RS leader (India: top 20% of Nifty 500 on 3- or 6-month return; US: RS line against SPY rising or at a new high). The stop must sit at a chart level, at least 1.5 × ATR away and within the setup's maximum width. Never add to a loser. The checklist is the app's 60-second check, and one failed item means skip.

**Equity basis for the journal tests:** the fresh-money tests, the 8% drawdown test and the 5% halving trigger are computed on new-trade equity only: starting capital plus the profit and loss of closed new trades, as the app's equity curve does. The legacy book is not in these numbers, so a bad week in the legacy holdings cannot fail the system test; track its give-back separately.

**MAE and MFE** are computed from evening closes (the best and worst close, in R), not from intraday highs and lows. A close-based MAE understates how often a stop was nearly hit, so correct it from the chart when closing a trade.

## Exits, journal and review

**Exit rules** (applied in order every evening to every open position; written for India with a broker GTT, the US equivalent is a stop order):

| # | Trigger | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Buy order filled | Same evening place a stop sell for the full quantity at the stop, no limit price |
| 2 | Price hits the stop | The stop sells. Never cancel it or move it lower |
| 3 | Failed breakout: closes back below the pivot within 3 sessions | Sell next morning |
| 4 | Time stop: 10 sessions without a close at +1R | Sell, the capital is idle |
| 5 | A close at +2R or better | Sell one third, move the stop on the rest to entry |
| 6 | Trail, once rule 5 has sold the third (C-68): weeks 1–7 first daily close below the 20 EMA; from week 8 first weekly close below the 10-week average | Sell the rest next morning |
| 7 | Extended, once rule 5 has sold the third: close 20% or more above the 20 EMA, or the biggest up-day of the move after 3+ weeks of gains | Sell another third |
| 8 | Results due within 2 sessions | Gain below 2R: exit. 2R or more: hold with the stop at entry |
| 9 | Regime drops a level | Positions below +1R: stop to today's low or the 10 EMA, whichever is higher. Above +1R keep the stop. No new buys |

Volume tests used by setups: breakout day at least 1.5× the stock's 50-day average volume; IPO base breakout 2×; earnings gap 3×. Setup 3 test (copied from the app Rules tab, OQ-7): a gap of 5% or more on 3× the 50-day average volume on results day, and the results show 25% or more sales or profit growth. Entry is the next day: trigger = gap-day high + 0.2%, limit = trigger + 1.5%. Stop = the gap-day low; skip the trade if the stop is more than 8% away, or if the gap came from a deal, block trade or rumour rather than results. For index distribution and follow-through days, volume only has to exceed the previous session; no session is skipped in either market (C-73).

**India-only mechanics:** skip stocks in the 2%, 5% or 10% price bands and any stock that hit a lower circuit in the last 3 months. After any bonus, split or ex-date, re-place stops at the adjusted price.

**US differences in exits:** the trail is a weekly close below the 10-week average from the start, so winners can run for months and approach the 24-month long-term tax clock. US sells go in before the next US open, and a stop is a stop order, not a GTT. The circuit-band and ASM rules are India only.

**Journal.** Each trade logs date, stock, setup, sector rank, regime, planned entry, fill, slippage, stop, shares, 1R, exit date and price, exit rule, R-multiple, MAE, MFE, whether rules were followed, and a note. Skipped setups are logged with the reason.

**Monthly review and the fresh-money test.** Fresh money is added only after at least 20 closed trades over at least 3 months pass all four tests:

| Test | Pass mark |
| --- | --- |
| Expectancy per trade | +0.3R or better |
| Average loss | 1.2R or smaller |
| Rule breaks | 2 or fewer in the last 20 trades |
| Drawdown from equity peak | Under 8% |

The tests also run per setup. A setup that fails alone is dropped. When all four pass in total, risk per trade may rise to 1% (India Green only; the US stays at 0.5%) and fresh money goes in over three monthly tranches, with the review re-run after each.

For stock RS, excluding the last two weeks still has support and is a challenger too | Whole-market closes, backtest | Baseline kept. Challenger waits for backtest (phase 6) |
| 2 | Rank industry groups by breadth (share of stocks above the 50 SMA, median RS percentile) instead of cap-weighted indices | Sound. Index leaders can be one or two heavy stocks, and past winners came from groups with no index. Depends on the whole-market store | C-20 store | Proposed |
| 3 | Build the whole-market universe before more work on the ETF-holdings screen | Agree. It is already C-20. A US universe source is not chosen yet | Source decision | Proposed |
| 4 | Quantify base quality: 10-day range divided by ATR below about 2, weekly closes within 3% over 3 weeks, up-day volume above down-day volume over 50 sessions | Useful to make the base test objective. Record the numbers on every candidate first and filter only if the journal shows they earn it | Whole-market data | Proposed |
| 5 | Prefer earnings acceleration (growth rising over 2 or 3 quarters) over a growth level | Plausible. Needs a reliable fundamentals source, which is a data-accuracy risk like the others | Fundamentals source | Parked |
| 6 | Rank by closeness to the 52-week high within the existing 25% rule | Cheap tie-break. Log it | Whole-market data | Proposed |
| 7 | A fixed, pre-registered candidate score (RS percentile, industry breadth, base tightness, distance to pivot, volume ratio, earnings acceleration) used when there are more candidates than slots | Good discipline. Record every factor on each candidate from day one, fix the weights before using them, and review after 20 trades | Candidate scan, journal fields | Proposed |
| 8 | Correlation guard: at most 50% of open risk in sectors whose 3-month returns correlate above 0.8 | The numbers 50% and 0.8 are untested guesses. The per-sector cap does not catch a single theme spread across sectors, so the idea is worth testing | Return history | Proposed |
| 9 | Score the base shape of shortlisted stocks only: fit a curve to a cup, measure flatness for a flat base, count shrinking pullbacks and volume for a contraction pattern, and show a small chart with the fit and a score | Practical because the shortlist is only 10 to 30 stocks a night. Patterns are loose descriptions, so a fit only approximates them and the thresholds are our choice. Record the scores only. Compare them with the owner's own yes or no on about 20 past charts (for example the Kaynes and PSU bank moves) before they change what is shown or filtered. Extends idea 4 | Whole-market daily prices, 20 labelled charts | Proposed, build phase 4 |

The review also says a well-run breakout system wins about 40 to 45% of trades and that most of the gap between a weak and a strong system comes from exits, sizing and regime discipline. I have not verified that figure; treat it as a reminder that ranking changes are marginal against the exit rules.

# Swing Desk – Code and Architecture (Source of Truth)

2026-10-03 · @Owner

## Purpose and how the two documents relate

This document says how the Swing Desk is built so a new engineer or an AI coding tool can run, fix and extend it without asking the original author. The companion Engine Rules document says what the desk decides and why. Rules change only through that document's Change log; this document describes the machinery that carries them out.

**Code version:** app v9.1 on Claude Artifacts (3 Oct 2026), patched from v9 to follow Engine Rules R-2026.10.5 (the repo's engine follows the version in `RULES_VERSION`, currently R-2026.10.9). The GitHub build has started in the private repo bpishigh/Swing_desk (phase 0: scaffold, fixtures, source test, Telegram alert, and a TypeScript engine replayed against v9; engine commit b6ae0f6, 3 Oct 2026). The live desk is v9.1 and still fed by the Claude scheduled tasks, so sections marked Target describe the intended design, not what runs.

**Reading order for a newcomer:** this section, the system map, data flow, schema, then the runbook. Read the Engine Rules before changing any calculation.

**Hard rules for anyone changing the code:**

1. No rule value is written in code. It comes from a settings file or table named in the Settings section. (Applies to the rewrite; app v9 still keeps them in constants.)
2. Every number shown to the trader carries a source and an as-of date. Missing or stale data is shown as missing, never filled in.
3. A change that alters a decision is logged in the Engine Rules Change log first.
4. In the Claude runtime, never retry or route around a 403 or 407 from the organisation proxy. On a GitHub runner, a 403 from a source such as NSE comes from the source itself: the right first response is standard browser headers and a session cookie on the first request, logged. Evasion such as rotating addresses or ignoring a site's stated terms is never acceptable. Record every block in the data quirks list.

## System map

Today the desk is one self-contained HTML app with a built-in database, filled by three scheduled Claude tasks. The target moves the fill and the app off Claude.

| Part | Today (app v9) | Target (GitHub build) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App | Single HTML file published as a Claude Artifact (swing-desk.html), rules and screens in one script | Static app on GitHub Pages, one rules module shared by India and US |
| Database | Artifact built-in database, collections listed in the Schema section | JSON files committed to the repo by the nightly job; where trades and the journal live depends on decision 3 below (browser storage is the weakest option) |
| India data fill | Claude task, nightly 21:40 IST weekdays, and morning 07:20 IST Tue–Sat | GitHub Actions script, nightly |
| US data fill | Same morning task; US sector pages, TipRanks SMAs, stored closes | GitHub Actions script, nightly, from verified sources only |
| US stock screen | Claude task, Saturday 08:41 IST, writes the us_screen collection | Same script as the daily scan, run nightly |
| Alerts | None | Telegram or ntfy message after each run and on failures |
| Checks | Manual look at stamps | Automated data-health checks that block a stale run from reaching the app |

**Scheduled tasks today:**

| Task | Id | Schedule | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| India nightly | trig_01PmtKhLn7Y14j5QRP791DMC | 21:40 IST, weekdays | Fill India feed and sector closes |
| Morning | trig_01LXdn6TvN5LNpFeAcdQvcGd | 07:20 IST, Tue–Sat | Fill US feed, compute returns and 200 SMAs from stored closes, top up history (max 2 gaps a run). Never uses an API key |
| US weekly screen | trig_01GLFkAY7uPtSXawEcXvAJVH | Saturday 08:41 IST, automatic approval | Build the us_screen document for the sectors in the top group |

The three task prompts are the code of today's data fill. They live inside the scheduled tasks and are not yet copied into this document or a repo, so export them with the fixtures (decision 9) before anything is changed. The Claude app, its database and the tasks are the only runtime. Decided 3 Oct 2026: app v9 stays the live desk on Claude while the GitHub build is made in a private repo, and the two run in parallel until the new data matches (scope of work, phases 1 and 2). If the Claude account or tasks stop, the data stops filling; that dependence is the main reason for the GitHub build.

## Data flow and schedule

**India, each weekday evening (21:40 IST):**

1. Download the official NSE index close file for the day (ind_close_all_DDMMYYYY.csv). Quirk seen on 3 Oct 2026: NSE's whole-market file (sec_bhavdata_full_DDMMYYYY.csv) can carry the previous session's data under a holiday's file name (the 02 Oct file held 01 Oct data), so the engine always reads the date inside the file and never trusts the filename.
2. Append the closes to the idx_closes history, then compute each sector's SMAs and 1- and 3-month returns from that history.
3. Write the feed document (collection feed, doc latest) and the dated tracker row (tracker).
4. The app reads feed and tracker on load and computes the regime under the Engine Rules. Breadth and similar regime inputs are typed in by the trader today (decision 5).

**US, each morning (07:20 IST, Tue–Sat, after the US close):**

1. Read sector ETF and SPY closes from the StockAnalysis pages (latest 50 rows).
2. Merge the rows into the stored closes document (us_feed_hist, doc closes), keyed by date. Existing dates are never overwritten.
3. Compute 1- and 3-month returns for every sector and for SPY from stored closes. Compute the 200 SMA from stored closes where 200 dates exist; otherwise use the TipRanks value and mark sma200Src.
4. Top up history from Yahoo date-windowed pages for at most 2 tickers with gaps, and stop on any HTTP 429.
5. Write us_feed (doc latest) with the date of the data, flags and the fetch time. A run that cannot confirm today's date writes a flag and leaves the previous values.

**US stock screen, Saturday 08:41 IST:** read the top-group sector ETFs from us_feed, pull each ETF's top 10 holdings, fetch each stock's recent history, compute the metrics listed in the Schema section, and write us_screen (doc latest).

**Target schedule (GitHub Actions):** India after the NSE file is published, US after the US close, whole-market scan nightly, each run followed by data-health checks and an alert.

## Data sources, checks and known quirks

Data accuracy has been the main failure of the desk, more than strategy. Each source below has a status, and a source may only feed a decision while its status is Used.

| Source | Used for | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NSE official index close file | India sector closes, SMAs, returns | Used | Complete and dated. Primary India source |
| StockAnalysis ETF pages | US sector ETF and SPY closes (50 rows) | Used | Latest 50 rows only, so history must be stored |
| Stored closes (us_feed_hist/closes) | US returns and 200 SMA | Used | Unadjusted closes, SPY dates as the calendar. Source of truth for US averages |
| TipRanks | US 50 and 200 SMA where no stored history | Interim | Stamps went stale; dividend-adjusted so 200 SMA runs up to about 1.3% lower than computed |
| Yahoo history, date-windowed pages | Top-up of stored closes | Parked | Complete rows but 9 of 32 requests returned 429. Slow top-up only |
| Yahoo full-page history | none | Rejected | Truncated and gappy when read through the Claude fetch tool. Re-test from GitHub (phase 0) |
| Yahoo chart API | none | Rejected | Blocked for the Claude fetch tool by robots rules, not necessarily by the source. Re-test from GitHub (phase 0) |
| Alpha Vantage | none | Rejected | 25 requests a day and a burst limit; owner said not to use the key. PROPOSED (owner decision, 3 Oct 2026, third review): the first probe showed Yahoo 429 and Stooq 403 from GitHub's servers, so the keyless US plan may not hold. The seven-day test now also probes free-tier keyed EOD APIs (Tiingo, Polygon, EODHD) and Yahoo with the cookie and crumb handshake; each key lives only in a GitHub secret and its probe is skipped when absent. The Alpha Vantage key stays unused. Owner approved Tiingo first, with Massive or EODHD as backup, and FRED for VIX, as a logged exception (3 Oct 2026); adoption for production waits on the test (history depth and cross-check) |
| ETF Database averages | none | Rejected | Values unreliable |
| Upstox and Dhan pages | India stock prices, volume, averages and EMAs for the held stocks | Used, with known gaps | The Dhan technical page was stale for a number of the held stocks on 1 Oct (Engine Rules OQ-6). To be replaced by averages computed from stored closes |
| StockAnalysis holdings, history and statistics | US screen: ETF holdings, stock history, 200 SMA, 52-week change, next results date | Used | The stock 200 SMA is the figure the page publishes, not computed here, and whether it is dividend-adjusted is not recorded. Results dates may be missing and are then flagged |
| TradingView and Chartink scans (manual) | Breadth, RS rank, trend template and volume scans | Manual | Run and typed in by the trader. The target replaces these with the whole-market store |

**Checks the pipeline must enforce (target; today partly manual):**

- Every stored value has a source name and an as-of date.
- A date earlier than the previous run's is a failed run, not new data.
- Closes must be unadjusted and must not jump more than a set percentage in a day without a corporate-action note (splits and bonuses corrupt averages otherwise).
- A computed SMA needs the full window of stored dates. Fewer means missing, not approximate.
- A run with a stale or missing source writes a flag and keeps the old values; it never writes zeros.

**Known quirks:**

- Computed 200 SMA differs from published figures by up to about 1.3% for dividend-paying ETFs. This is expected (Engine Rules C-14).
- In the Claude runtime a 403 or 407 means the organisation proxy blocks that site; do not retry or route around it. On GitHub, treat a 403 as the source's own response and follow hard rule 4.
- A 429 means the source is rate limiting. The response asks not to refetch; stop and move on.
- Summaries of fetched pages can report wrong row counts. Count rows in the stored data, not in the summary.
- GitHub servers may be blocked by NSE or Yahoo. None of the target data sources has been tested from GitHub yet; do this first in build phase 0.

## Data schema

The app database is a set of collections of documents keyed by id. In the US market the app adds the prefix us_ to the collections marked in the last column; India uses the bare name. Writes to an existing document need the document's version (if_version), or they are rejected.

| regime | date | saved regime inputs: n50, n500 (green, mixed or red), dist, breadth, ftd, expiry. Empty today; the regime is computed from tracker rows | yes |

| feed_hist | date (India); closes (US) | India: one snapshot per day with bench, sectors, stocks. US: the stored closes used to compute returns and averages | yes |
| trades | trade id | planned, open and closed trades (fields below). Empty today | yes |
| logs | log id | skipped setups (type skip) and no-trade weeks (type notrade) with date, reason and outcome. Empty today | yes |

## Settings and configuration

**Today (app v9):** rule values live in constants near the top of the app script. Changing a rule means editing the script, which is the thing the target design removes.

| Constant | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| SETUPS | Per setup: trigger %, limit %, max stop width, basis text, stop hint, flags (breakout, ipo, resultsExempt) |
| LIMITS (India), LIMITS_US | Per regime: allowed setups, number of top sectors, risk per trade %, max positions, and cap (the maximum total open risk for new trades as a % of capital, not a position cap; to be renamed maxOpenRiskPct in the rewrite). Red setups must change to pilots only in v10 (Engine Rules OQ-8) |
| SECTORS, SECTORS_US | Sector names and the index or ETF used for each |
| IDX | Benchmark names per market (US: SPY, QQQ; India: Nifty 50, Nifty 500) |
| EXIT_RULES | Exit rule names recorded in the journal |
| SCR_MIN_ADV, SCR_MIN_RESULTS | US screen liquidity floor ($50 million) and results-date gap (10 trading days) |

**Target:** one settings file per market (settings/india.json, settings/us.json) holding every value above plus the room multiple (3R US, 2R India), the 1.5 ATR stop floor, distribution-day and breadth thresholds, VIX threshold, liquidity floors and the source list. Both files share one schema (settings/schema.json), so a value that exists for one market must exist for the other, even when equal. The app and the scripts read the same files. Each file carries a rulesVersion field that must match the current Engine Rules version; a mismatch fails the build and is shown on the screen footer.

**Secrets:** none in the app. The target alert tokens live in GitHub repository secrets. Logged exception to the no-API-key rule (owner decision, 3 Oct 2026): US end-of-day data may use Tiingo as the primary source, Massive (the former Polygon) or EODHD as the backup, and FRED for a VIX cross-check (FRED lags a day; Cboe's free VIX history file needs no key and is the candidate primary VIX source, pending the seven-day test), each key held only as a GitHub repository secret (TIINGO_KEY, POLYGON_KEY, EODHD_KEY, FRED_KEY), never in the repo, the app or the data files. The India feed stays keyless. The Alpha Vantage key stays unused. A key is adopted for production only after the seven-day source test shows the free plan returns 200 or more days of history and its newest SPY close agrees with the second source within 0.1%. The EMA length is 20 everywhere: the feed field is ema20 and the screen computes a 20-period EMA. The app code still names a local variable ema21, a leftover to rename in the rewrite.

## Target repository layout

This layout is a proposal for the GitHub build, to be confirmed in build phase 0. It keeps rules, data, scripts and app apart.

**Actual layout so far (3 Oct 2026), where it differs from the target above:** TypeScript on Node 22 with type stripping and no dependencies, not a separate language per layer. The engine is `src/engine/` (indicators, regime, sectors, setups, sizing, checklist, exits, journal, book, legacy, proposals, format, settings) and is pure functions with no I/O. Tests are in `test/`. `fixtures/` holds the market files from the live database (`db/`), the v9 a`nd v9.1 app files (app/, with test/app-parity.test.ts checking v9.1 against the engine`), the golden outputs of v9's own code (`expected/`) and the scheduled-task prompts (`scheduled-tasks/`). `tools/` holds the golden generators, `scripts/` the source test, alert sender and privacy check, `docs/review-notes/` one review note per engine block. Rule values are still in code (`setups.ts`); the switches and parameters for rules that are still Proposed (C-29 to C-34) are in `src/engine/settings.ts`, all off. The two source-of-truth docs are copied into the repo as docs/ENGINE_RULES.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (exported from the live docs with tools/doc-xml-to-md.mjs). The live docs stay the source of truth: after any change to either doc, re-export the copy and commit it in the same step; a test fails if the rules version in the code and in the copy differ. Nothing personal (capital, holdings, trades) is in the repo; a test blocks it from `data/` and `fixtures/db/`.

The two docs stay the master copies. A job in the repo fails if docs/ENGINE_RULES.md carries a different rules version from settings/*.json.

## Testing, runbook and failure handling

**Testing today:** the US screen was tested with a headless browser against seeded data (test_ui.js checks the panel renders; test_plan.js checks that Plan this trade fills the New trade form for a stock). Calculations were checked against stored closes. There is no automated test of the India path.

**Testing target:** unit tests for every function in the engine using fixtures from real days; a replay test that feeds a saved run through the engine and compares the regime, the ranking and the screen with saved answers; a data-health test per source; any change to a rule value fails the tests until the Engine Rules version is bumped.

**Testing progress (3 Oct 2026):** 98 tests pass in CI on every push. Seven engine blocks are replayed against the original v9 code run over seeded random inputs (regime, sector ranking, sizing, checklist, exits, journal, book and legacy numbers), plus tests that quote the rule text and, for Proposed rules, hand-built cases. A replay proves the port equals v9, not that v9's rules are right. Still to do: replay the engine over stored real days once the source test has produced them (Gate B), and the ten-session parallel run per market (Gate A).

**Runbook, when something looks wrong:**

1. Check the as-of dates on the feed. A stale date means the fill did not run or the source did not update.
2. Check the run log of the failing job (today the task's run history; target the Actions run) for a 403, 407 or 429. Those mean blocked or rate limited: follow hard rule 4 and record it in the quirks list.
3. Compare one sector's computed 200 SMA with the stored closes count. Fewer than 200 dates means the value is a fallback and flagged.
4. If a value is wrong and the source is right, fix the compute step and add a test with that day's data.
5. If the source is wrong, add or change an override, log it, and open a Change log entry if a rule has to change.

**Failure handling:** a failed run keeps the previous good data and raises a flag; it never writes zeros or guesses. Today, tasks have no self-healing and nobody is alerted. The target sends a Telegram or ntfy alert on any failed or stale run.

**Checked on 3 Oct 2026:** the India feed is dated 1 Oct, which is right because 2 Oct was a holiday and 3 Oct is a Saturday. The US feed holds 2 Oct data, written at 07:25 IST on 3 Oct, so the morning run worked. The India nightly run of 1 Oct finished in about 40 seconds and the feed carries flags that some stocks have stale EMAs (Dhan technical page) and two prices came from an earlier run, so that run may have under-fetched; this is open item OQ-6 in the Engine Rules. Five US sectors still use TipRanks 200 SMAs with stale stamps until the history top-up completes.

## Handover checklist and glossary

**Before handing this to a person or an AI tool:**

- [ ] Both documents are current: the Engine Rules version matches the code, and the Change log has every decision to date.
- [ ] The open items in the Engine Rules (OQ-5, OQ-6, OQ-7, OQ-8) are closed or assigned.
- [ ] The schema is formalised as a JSON schema file and a test checks saved documents against it (field lists are written out in this document today).
- [ ] The repo layout above is built and the tests pass.
- [ ] Every data source has been run from the real runner (GitHub servers) and its status in the sources table is current.
- [ ] Scheduled jobs, alert channels and where secrets are kept are listed with who owns each.
- [ ] The new owner has run the runbook once on a deliberately stale feed.

**For an AI coding tool:** give it both documents, the repo, and the instruction to change a rule only by writing the Change log row first and to update the tests with the change.

**Glossary:**

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| R, 1R | The money risked on a trade, the distance from entry to stop times shares |
| ATR | Average true range, the typical daily price swing, here over 14 sessions |
| SMA, EMA | Simple and exponential moving averages, for example 50 SMA, 20 EMA |
| Regime, traffic light | Green, Yellow or Red market state that sets how much risk is allowed |
| Distribution day | A day the index falls on higher volume, a sign of selling |
| Follow-through day | A strong up-day on rising volume after a correction, a sign of recovery |
| Setup | A named pattern for entering a stock (base breakout, pullbacks, earnings gap) |
| Pivot | The price above which a base breaks out |
| Persistence | A sector holding a top rank on two consecutive weekends |
| MAE, MFE | Worst and best points of a trade versus entry, in R |
| Feed | The data the fill jobs write for the app to read |
| Source of truth | The one document or file that wins when copies disagree |
| Pilot | A trade at reduced risk (0.25%) in a Red market, an early sector or a new leader |
| GTT, AMO | India broker orders: a standing trigger order, and an after-market order placed for the next morning |
| RS, RS leader | Relative strength against the market; a leader is in the top 20% (India) or has its RS line rising against SPY (US) |
| Legacy book | The owner's older India holdings, managed by an exit test and a separate risk budget, not by the new-trade rules |
| Bhavcopy | NSE's daily file of every listed stock's prices and volume |

## Decisions to make before the build

Added after the first review on 3 Oct 2026. Each one changes the design if it goes the other way, so settle them before phase 1.

| # | Decision | Why it matters | Recommendation | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Source test from the real runner (phase 0) | NSE may block cloud servers, and several sources were rejected only because of the Claude fetch tool or the organisation proxy, not the source. Yahoo chart, stooq and Tiingo's free tier are untested from GitHub | A throwaway workflow calls every candidate source daily for a week and logs the status code. If NSE blocks GitHub, India runs on a small VPS or a cron on the owner's own machine | India runner decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner): GitHub, reviewed on Sat 10 Oct from the week's log (scripts/summarise-source-test.mjs prints the verdict). Success means HTTP 200 and the file's internal date (dataDate) equals the session date, because NSE has served the previous session under a new day's filename; a 200 with a stale date is a failure. Switch to a small server or the owner's machine if any one of these holds: (1) on any weekday the index-close file was not fetched with the right date by 23:00 IST, which leaves one more poll before the 23:30 deadline; (2) any single weekday where every NSE probe returned 403 or 429 (a full-day block); (3) 403 or 429 on two or more different days (intermittent). Two isolated 429s on different days at the first probe of the window, with success later in the same window, are normal for NSE and do not trigger a switch by themselves. The IST time the file first appears with the right date is logged each day and sets the production polling window. The choice is cheap to reverse: the scripts are plain Node with no dependencies and run unchanged from any scheduler. No rule changes, so nothing in the Engine Rules. Status of the test (3 Oct 2026): probes run from GitHub every 30 minutes on weekdays; first full week is Mon 5 to Fri 9 Oct, summary due Sat 10 Oct. GitHub stays the India runner unless that week shows blocks, and the week must include at least one successful fetch of the index-close file inside the nightly window, because the regime depends on it and it has not yet been observed from GitHub. First result: NSE bhavcopy, event calendar and Nifty 500 list answered 200; Yahoo chart returned 429; Stooq 403 |
| 2 | Hosting and privacy | GitHub Pages is public on the free plan, so committed data would publish holdings, capital and trades | Keep personal data out of any public repo: private repo with Cloudflare Pages behind a login, or a local app | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner): private repo on the free GitHub plan, so Pages cannot serve it. Recommended: Cloudflare Pages behind a free login (Cloudflare Access), deployed from the private repo. Confirmed by owner 3 Oct 2026 |
| 3 | Where trades and journal persist | Browser storage is lost with the browser profile, and the fresh-money test depends on the journal | Commit trades through the GitHub API to a private repo, or use a small hosted database | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner): closed trades and the journal are committed to the private repo through the GitHub API; browser storage is only a cache |
| 4 | One language for the engine | If the app is JavaScript and the jobs are Python, two engines drift apart | Write the engine in TypeScript, run the nightly jobs in Node, and import the same module in the app | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
| 5 | India breadth | Today breadth is a manual scan feeding tracker.b, so the regime depends on a number typed each night | Store the NSE daily bhavcopy (whole-market closes) and compute breadth and the whole-market scan from it; build this store first | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
| 6 | Corporate actions for single stocks | Unadjusted closes are right for index ETFs but wrong across a split or bonus, which breaks a stock's 200 SMA and 52-week high for a year | Use the NSE corporate actions file to adjust or flag; set the maximum unexplained daily move in phase 1 | Open |
| 7 | Correcting a bad close | Never overwriting a stored date means one bad fetch is permanent | Allow a logged, flagged re-fetch of a named date | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
| 8 | Market calendars | Skipped days for expiry, rebalancing, holidays and Muhurat need a source | A holiday and special-day file per market in settings, updated yearly, used by the tests | Decided 3 Oct 2026 (owner) |
